title: Sliding Window Maximum
statement: A window of size k slides one step at a time from the left end of the list to the right end. Return the maximum value inside the window at each position.
brute_force_solution:
def maxSlidingWindow(nums, k):
    return [max(nums[i:i + k]) for i in range(len(nums) - k + 1)]

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(11)
    return [[r.randint(-10**6, 10**6) for _ in range(100000)], 30000]

hints.1_question: As the window slides, which elements could ever become the maximum later, and which can be forgotten forever?
hints.2_nudge: Keep a deque of indices whose values are in decreasing order. A new value makes every smaller value before it useless.
hints.3_big_hint: For each i: pop from the back while nums[back] <= nums[i]; push i; pop from the front if it left the window (index <= i - k); once i >= k-1 record nums[front].

known_bugs.name: never removes indices that left the window
known_bugs.followup: Your front element may belong to a position the window has already passed. Where do you check that?

known_bugs.name: starts recording before the window is full
known_bugs.followup: How many windows are there in an array of n elements with window size k, and how many outputs does your loop produce?

known_bugs.name: takes max() of every slice (O(n*k))
